claims.summary: For alpha_1, alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2 >= 1/2, u_j = (log N)^(1/alpha_j), s_0 = sqrt(log N/N), X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, Y evenly spread or an independent uniform sample, and K the constant of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold: (a) with probability tending to one some matching has X_i - Y_pi(i) in B(X_i) for every i, simultaneously for every box family x -> B(x) (any shape, varying with position, N or the sample; an argument with boxes at several scales is read with their intersection) with B(x) containing [-K u_1 s_0, K u_1 s_0] x [-K u_2 s_0, K u_2 s_0] at every x; (b) hence no argument concluding that every matching has a pair outside such a family is correct, and a refutation of a pair of the curve by one pair's exit, which needs boxes containing the conjecture's maximum box for every L, fails at every L >= K.
claims.assessment: Working proof: the containment step on the event of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold, which does not depend on the family, and its contrapositive. Elementary.
claims.rationale: Closes the queued item varying-aspect-subgraphs in its maximal-displacement reading, superseded on 16 October by thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold: Leighton-Shor subgraph arguments with any scaling across the tent scales cannot refute a pair of the curve through one exit; a count reading implies a refutation of the mixed-level count question at some pair of levels, up to a factor (floor(log N)+1)^2 in the count and e in the allowance, pairs of equal levels falling under thm:per-level-count-matchings.
claims.next_action: None for this corollary; the count reading joins the queued item mixed-level-counts.

relationships: Its event and matching give (a); the corollary states that theorem's consequence for box families of every shape.
Below the curve one scaled Leighton-Shor exit refutes; on and above it no exit from boxes containing the threshold box can.
